Predominant Mineralocorticoid Deficiency in ZNRF3-Related Adrenal Hypoplasia Congenita: A case report.
abstract: Introduction E3 ubiquitin protein ligase zinc and ring finger 3 (ZNRF3) negatively regulates Wnt/β-catenin signaling, which is essential for the development and maintenance of the adrenal gland, particularly the zona glomerulosa. Heterozygous ZNRF3 exon 2 deletions cause adrenal hypoplasia congenita (AHC). However, as only a few patients with ZNRF3-related AHC have been reported, the clinical spectrum remains unclear. Case Presentation A girl presented at age 27 days with severe salt-wasting. Endocrinological evaluation revealed elevated ACTH and renin levels. Abdominal ultrasonography failed to detect the adrenal glands. After treatment with hydrocortisone and fludrocortisone, she had no adrenal crises and normal growth and puberty. At age 15 years, hydrocortisone was discontinued, while fludrocortisone was continued. ACTH levels remained within clinically acceptable limits, whereas renin levels remained elevated. Whole-genome sequencing identified a ZNRF3 exon 2 deletion. Conclusion This is the first report of longitudinal endocrine findings in ZNRF3-related AHC, demonstrating predominant and persistent zona glomerulosa dysfunction with age-dependent improvement of zona fasciculata function. Our findings support the proposed role of the ZNRF3-Wnt/β-catenin signaling axis in adrenal development, expand the phenotypic spectrum of ZNRF3-related AHC, and suggest the value of genetic screening for ZNRF3 exon 2 deletions in patients with genetically unresolved mineralocorticoid deficiency.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Paediatric Endocrinology: A Narrative Review from the Perspective of Early-career Clinicians and Researchers.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Artificial intelligence (AI) use by early-career paediatric endocrinologists has started without waiting for the training and governance structures to develop. Since early-career physicians and researchers of today hold no pre-AI performance baseline against which to appraise the AI outputs, career stage-specific concerns regarding rapid adoption of AI use in the field have emerged. The goal of this review was to examine AI use in paediatric endocrinology from the early-career perspective.
SUMMARY: A narrative, non-systematic literature review regarding the AI use in paediatric endocrinology across the four professional domains (curricular coverage, clinical practice, teaching, and research) was conducted in January 2026 and updated through July 2026. 57 relevant publications were identified, with level of evidence differing significantly between domains, and inversely with how freely the AI tools are used: from randomised-trials data regarding specific clinical applications like closed-loop insulin delivery and automated bone age assessment, to no published data regarding use of large language models in the research domain. Greatest benefit of automated bone age assessment in the early career stage was reported, while no published studies examining AI use by early-career paediatric endocrinologists were found.
KEY MESSAGES: While being most exposed to unsupervised AI use, early-career physicians are also the least studied group. Having in mind the lack of pre-AI baseline in this population, findings of this review emphasize the potential career stage-dependent risks regarding the AI use, and the need for subspecialty-specific AI competency frameworks.

title: When Less is More: A Physiology-Driven Approach to a 17-Hydroxylase Deficiency Case Series.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: 17-hydroxylase deficiency (17OHD) is a very rare form of congenital adrenal hyperplasia (CAH) caused by autosomal recessive mutations in the cytochrome P450 family (CYP17A1). Despite low cortisol, adrenal insufficiency does not typically manifest because elevated corticosterone, a weaker glucocorticoid (GC), exerts GC effects. Exogenous GC are the foundation of treatment but can be associated with significant side effects. Published literature regarding management strategies is limited.
CASE PRESENTATIONS: We describe three female adolescents treated for 17OHD with different GC regimens. All patients presented at age 14 with delayed puberty, hypertension, and primary ovarian insufficiency. Patient 1 was initially treated with physiological hydrocortisone divided three times daily (10 mg/m2/d) and spironolactone 100 mg/d, separately and combined, which did not lower her blood pressure (BP). Eventually, a combination of physiological hydrocortisone once daily (8.8 mg/m2/d) and gradual titration to a higher spironolactone dose (100 mg bid) normalized her BP (115/75 mmHg) with no side effects. Patient 2 was treated with dexamethasone 0.25 mg daily for 10 years with poor follow-up and developed multiple complications related to supraphysiological GC use. She was transitioned and successfully treated with hydrocortisone 10 mg every morning and 5 mg every afternoon with a normal BP and potassium for over a year. Patient 3 was treated with cortisone acetate for 2.6 years and then with dexamethasone for about 10 months before discontinuation of GC and transition to spironolactone monotherapy. Her potassium and BP remained normal.
CONCLUSION: In conclusion, 17OHD is a rare form of CAH, with about 500 published cases and limited established management guidance. Our cases highlight the importance of considering the pathophysiology of 17OHD when developing a management plan; a supraphysiological GC therapy may not be necessary to manage the hypertension and hypokalemia. Physiological hydrocortisone dosing lowers but does not normalize DOC production allowing DOC to exert GC effects. Physiological hydrocortisone and/or monotherapy with mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists both mitigate GC-related side effects, avoid adrenal suppression, and minimize risk for adrenal crisis in patients with 17OHD.

title: Pregestational maternal diabetes primes neonatal beta cell dysfunction with structural remodelling, impaired calcium buffering and altered mTORC2-Gαq-PKCα signalling in a pig model.
abstract:
AIMS/HYPOTHESIS: Offspring of mothers with diabetes are at increased risk of developing type 2 diabetes, and this predisposition is established during fetal life. The aim of this study was to define the functional, morphological and molecular alterations in neonatal pancreatic islets associated with maternal hyperglycaemia, with a particular focus on beta cells, an area that remains poorly understood. Given its similarity to humans in endocrine pancreas development, the pig was used as a translational animal model.
METHODS: Using genetically diabetic and beta cell reporter pig models, we performed functional assessments of glucose-stimulated insulin secretion in vivo and in situ using fresh pancreatic tissue slices from neonatal piglets born to hyperglycaemic mothers (PHGs) or normoglycaemic mothers (PNGs). Morphological and molecular profiling, including proteomics and single-cell RNA-seq, were performed to elucidate molecular changes reflecting the developmental impact of maternal diabetes on offspring metabolic health, with a particular focus on neonatal beta cells.
RESULTS: PHGs were born hyperglycaemic, hyperinsulinaemic and insulin resistant, exhibiting markedly delayed glucose and insulin response curves following oral glucose administration, with more pronounced effects in male piglets. Elevated basal insulin secretion and an almost blunted glucose responsiveness of pancreatic tissue slices were associated with increased insulin and somatostatin content, expansion of beta (+35%) and delta (+47%) cell populations, and organisation into larger islet clusters. Neonatal PHG islets exhibited a molecular profile consistent with intrinsic beta cell dysfunction that partially overlapped with type 2 diabetes (e.g. RBP4 upregulation), together with alterations in glucose sensing (near absence of GLUT2), nutrient metabolism resembling congenital hyperinsulinism (HADH downregulation), and cytosolic Ca2⁺ homeostasis (near absence of the Ca2⁺ buffer calbindin D28K). In addition to an ATF4-dominated stress signature, a shift towards a distinct PHG beta cell subcluster characterised by low expression of ribosomal genes was observed, with an adaptive early-response-gene-mediated transcriptional reactivity. In contrast to the Gαs-adenylyl cyclase-cAMP-PKA signalling axis that dominated in PNG beta cells, neonatal PHG beta cells displayed distinct alterations in Gαq-PLC-PKCα signalling components, the mTORC2 target PKCα, and CREB1, suggesting a restructured signalling architecture.
CONCLUSIONS/INTERPRETATION: Our findings reveal altered islet modelling with a unique beta cell dysfunction profile that partially overlaps with, but differs from, that of type 2 diabetes. A shift towards a beta cell subcluster exhibiting an adaptive early-response-gene-mediated transcriptional reactivity and an ATF4-associated transcriptional stress signature provides insight into molecular alterations associated with fetal exposure to maternal diabetes and may contribute to the increased risk of metabolic disease in offspring.

title: Co-creating the EndoWatch - a smart wearable device for the management of hypothalamic dysfunction in pediatric brain tumor survivors: a pilot study.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Hypothalamic dysfunction (HD) after treatment for a pediatric (supra)sellar tumor severely affects quality of life of patients, as well as their parents and families. Patients may develop signs of fatigue as a result of persistent disturbances in thermoregulation, sleep-wake rhythm, or hormonal insufficiencies. The management of HD requires around-the-clock care by the parent or caregiver. To support patients with HD and their parents/caregivers, we co-created a smart wearable device for continuous monitoring (EndoWatch) to detect early signs of hypothalamic dysregulation. We aimed to evaluate adherence to and user experiences of the first EndoWatch design.
METHODS: In co-creation with clinicians, patient representatives, and design researchers and engineers, an existing smart device (wearable sensor and mobile application (app)) was adapted to a first design tailored for this purpose. In a prospective, observational study, 10 pediatric brain tumor survivors with HD (8 children; 2 adults) tested the first design of the device for 14 days. The primary outcome was adherence to wearing the EndoWatch. Secondary outcomes included usability, learnability, and desirability (through questionnaires), and barriers and facilitators (through semi-structured interviews).
RESULTS: Ten patients participated (8 children, mean age 10.8 (SD 3.5); 2 adults, aged 18.9 and 31.0 years). Median overall adherence was 99.4% (IQR 22.8); two patients discontinued early due to wristband-related discomfort. Key facilitators were ease of use of the device and reliable technical performance. Main barriers included the absence of a separate caregiver app and limitations of the patient diary. These findings informed design modifications for future improvements of the device.
DISCUSSION: The concept of the first EndoWatch design was considered acceptable and usable by patients with HD and their caregivers. This study identified key barriers and the modifications required for improvement, which were incorporated into a second EndoWatch design, to be evaluated in a larger prospective study.

title: Isolated Hyperchlorhidrosis Caused by Novel Biallelic CA12 Variants Mimicking Pseudohypoaldosteronism.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Isolated hyperchlorhidrosis (HYCHL; OMIM 143860) is caused by biallelic CA12 variants encoding carbonic anhydrase XII (CA XII), a transmembrane enzyme that mediates sodium and chloride reabsorption in sweat glands, leading to excessive salt loss. Clinically, HYCHL presents in infancy with recurrent hyponatremic dehydration secondary to excessive salt loss, often mimicking pseudohypoaldosteronism (PHA) or cystic fibrosis (CF).
CASE PRESENTATION: A 5-month-old girl presented with irritability, lethargy, poor feeding, severe hyponatremia (110 mEq/L), and hyperkalemia (7.1 mEq/L). Congenital adrenal hyperplasia was excluded by endocrine evaluation. Markedly elevated plasma renin activity and aldosterone initially suggested PHA; however, low urinary sodium excretion during hyponatremia indicated an extrarenal source of salt loss. Three further episodes occurred, predominantly during summer. Although the parents consistently reported a salty taste of the infant's skin. Clinical exome sequencing identified two unreported compound heterozygous CA12 missense variants, c.823C>T p.(Arg275Trp) and c.694C>A p.(Pro232Thr), with parental testing confirming trans inheritance. No pathogenic variants were detected in CFTR or PHA-associated genes. By 19 months of age, the patient had remained free of hyponatremic episodes for nine months without disease-specific treatment, with normal growth and neurodevelopment.
CONCLUSION: This case expands the mutational spectrum of isolated hyperchlorhidrosis by identifying two unreported variants in CA12 and highlights the importance of considering isolated hyperchlorhidrosis in infants with recurrent salt-wasting when routine evaluation does not support PHA or CF.

title: A commentary on "An update on the genetic causes and treatment of hypophosphatemic rickets".
An update on the genetic causes and treatment of hypophosphatemic rickets.
abstract: Hypophosphatemic rickets (HR) results from impaired renal phosphate reabsorption caused either by genetic defects in renal phosphate cotransporters or by increased levels of phosphaturic mediators (phosphatonins). Fibroblast growth factor 23 (FGF23) is the principal regulator of phosphate metabolism and interacts with several hormonal and molecular pathways to maintain phosphate homeostasis. Variants in genes such as PHEX, FGF23, DMP1, ENPP1, FAM20C, and others lead to inherited forms of HR, and HR may also occur as part of several syndromic conditions. Affected patients typically present with short stature, skeletal deformities, bone pain, muscle weakness, dental abnormalities, and characteristic radiographic abnormalities. Laboratory findings usually include hypophosphatemia, normal or mildly elevated parathyroid hormone levels, and markedly increased alkaline phosphatase. Conventional therapy with oral phosphate and active vitamin D improves many metabolic abnormalities but rarely leads to full correction. The development of burosumab, a monoclonal antibody targeting FGF23, has transformed treatment by improving biochemical parameters, rickets severity, growth, and quality of life. This review summarizes current knowledge regarding the molecular mechanisms, clinical manifestations, diagnostic work-up, classification, and treatment strategies for HR, with particular emphasis on advances in targeted therapy.

title: Diabetes-related distress and perspectives on disability registration in pancreatic endocrine dysfunction: a multicenter web-based survey in Korea.
abstract:
PURPOSE: This study aimed to assess diabetes-related distress and perspectives on disability registration among people with type 1 diabetes and other forms of pancreatic endocrine dysfunction (PED) and caregivers of pediatric patients in Korea.
METHODS: A multicenter web-based survey included individuals with type 1 diabetes or those who had undergone pancreatectomy or pancreas transplantation; caregivers responded on behalf of pediatric participants when applicable. Diabetes-related distress was assessed using the Diabetes Distress Scale (DDS), with a score ≥3 indicating elevated diabetes-related distress. Multivariable regression analyses were performed to identify factors associated with distress and perspectives on disability registration.
RESULTS: A total of 852 respondents (median patient age, 19.0 years; 49.2% aged ≤18 years; 98.5% with type 1 diabetes) were included. The median DDS score was 3.2 (interquartile range, 2.7-3.7), and 64.8% had a DDS score ≥3. Questionnaires concerning adult participants more frequently had DDS scores ≥3 than those concerning pediatric participants (69.8% vs. 59.6%, P=0.002). Emotional burden was the predominant domain (88.5% scoring ≥3). Overall, 97.1% of participants supported disability registration. Older age (B=-0.013), shorter duration of diabetes (B=-0.012), and diabetes-related complications (B=0.395) were associated with higher distress. Higher DDS scores were associated with support for disability registration (odds ratio, 2.89; 95% confidence interval, 1.64-5.11).
CONCLUSION: Diabetes-related distress is common in people with type 1 diabetes and other forms of PED, with emotional burden being particularly prominent. Higher DDS scores were associated with more favorable views of disability registration, suggesting that perceived psychosocial burden may influence perspectives on formal recognition and support.

title: Contemporary age at menarche among Thai girls: a nationwide cross-sectional study and its public health implications.
abstract:
PURPOSE: Age at menarche has declined globally. However, contemporary population-level data from Southeast Asia remain limited. This study aimed to characterize menarcheal timing among Thai schoolgirls and identify associated factors using survival-based methods.
METHODS: A nationwide cross-sectional study was conducted among 8,161 Thai schoolgirls in grades 3-9. Menarcheal status and age at menarche were assessed using questionnaires and verified by caregivers. Kaplan-Meier survival analysis was used to estimate the cumulative probability of menarche by age, accounting for right-censoring. Determinants of menarcheal timing were examined using Cox proportional hazards regression models.
RESULTS: At assessment, 52.6% of participants had attained menarche. Kaplan-Meier analysis demonstrated that the cumulative probability of menarche rose from 5.56% at 10 years to 85.21% at 13 years, with a median age of 12.0 years (interquartile range, 11.2-12.7 years). Based on survival-derived percentiles, early menarche (approximately <5th percentile) was defined as occurring before 10 years of age. Significant regional differences in menarcheal timing were observed (log-rank test, P<0.001). In multivariable Cox regression analysis, overweight (hazard ratio [HR], 1.67), obesity (HR, 1.64), and high socioeconomic status (HR, 1.28) were independently associated with earlier menarche, whereas underweight status was associated with delayed menarche (HR, 0.45; all P<0.001). After adjustment, only the Southern region remained significantly associated with later menarche compared with Bangkok.
CONCLUSION: Nutritional status and socioeconomic factors are key factors associated with menarcheal timing in Thailand. Survival-based, percentile-defined thresholds provide a useful framework for identifying atypical pubertal timing and may inform population-level public health strategies.

title: Maternal and perinatal factors associated with cord blood thyroid-stimulating hormone levels: a cross-sectional study.
abstract:
PURPOSE: Congenital hypothyroidism (CH) is the most common preventable cause of intellectual disability in children. Umbilical cord blood thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) is used for neonatal screening, but maternal and perinatal influences on cord blood TSH remain incompletely understood. This study aimed to identify maternal and perinatal factors associated with cord blood TSH levels.
METHODS: A descriptive, cross-sectional study was conducted among 1,088 consecutive live births at a tertiary hospital in South India (January-December 2022). Cord blood samples were analyzed for TSH using an electrochemiluminescence immunoassay. Maternal and neonatal characteristics were recorded, and associations with cord blood TSH were assessed. Neonates with cord blood TSH >20 μIU/mL were recalled for confirmatory serum thyroid function testing.
RESULTS: The median cord blood TSH was 7.22 μIU/mL, with an interquartile range of 5.39-10.28. Elevated cord blood TSH (>20 μIU/mL) was found in 5.9% of neonates. In unadjusted analyses, higher TSH levels were associated with primiparity, gestational diabetes, gestational hypertension, vaginal delivery, assisted delivery, and lower Apgar scores (P<0.05). Maternal TSH was positively correlated with cord blood TSH (r=0.193, P=0.002). No associations were observed with neonatal sex, gestational age, birth weight, or maternal anemia. Cord blood TSH showed modest positive correlations with postnatal day-3 serum TSH and free thyroxine.
CONCLUSION: Maternal thyroid status, parity, pregnancy complications, and mode of delivery are significantly associated with cord blood TSH. These factors should be considered when interpreting neonatal screening results for CH.

title: Triptorelin-stimulated gonadotropin concentrations for precocious puberty.
abstract:
PURPOSE: Subcutaneous triptorelin stimulation testing is used to evaluate girls with early breast development when intravenous gonadotropin-releasing hormone is unavailable, but the optimal sampling times and minimum test duration remain uncertain.
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 186 girls younger than 8 years who presented with breast development and underwent subcutaneous triptorelin testing (0.1 mg), with serum luteinizing hormone (LH) and follicle-stimulating hormone measured at 0, 30, 60, 90, and 120 minutes. Central precocious puberty (CPP) was defined as peak LH ≥5.0 IU/L; those below this threshold were classified as premature thelarche (PT). We performed receiver operating characteristic analyses for stimulated LH at 30, 60, 90, and 120 minutes and compared LH trajectories using mixed-effects modeling.
RESULTS: CPP was identified in 88 girls (47.3%). Using the 5.0 IU/L threshold, cumulative detection reached 90.9% by 60 minutes, 95.5% by 90 minutes, and 100% only by 120 minutes. Peak timing differed between groups: LH peaked mainly at 30-60 minutes in the CPP group (33.0% at 60 minutes; 29.5% at 30 minutes) and at 120 minutes in the PT group (51.0%). Diagnostic discrimination was excellent at all time points (area under the curve, 0.993-0.999), and LH trajectories differed significantly between groups (group-by-time interaction, P<0.001).
CONCLUSION: Although stimulated LH showed excellent discrimination at each sampled time point, sampling through 120 minutes was required to maximize sensitivity and minimize false-negative classification using a peak LH threshold of 5.0 IU/L.

The phenotypic spectrum of McCune-Albright syndrome: a report of four paediatric cases and a literature review.
abstract:
OBJECTIVES: McCune-Albright syndrome (MAS) is a rare mosaic disorder caused by postzygotic activating variants in GNAS, resulting in constitutive activation of stimulatory G protein alpha subunit (Gsα) signalling. The phenotype classically includes fibrous dysplasia, café-au-lait macules and hyperfunctioning endocrinopathies, but the clinical spectrum extends beyond this triad. We describe four paediatric cases and review the current literature, with emphasis on the diagnostic challenges of mosaicism, endocrine morbidity and evolving treatment.
CASE PRESENTATION: The four cases comprise a boy with polyostotic fibrous dysplasia, hyperthyroidism and Sertoli-cell hyperplasia; a girl with early fractures, peripheral precocious puberty, suspected phosphate wasting and craniofacial fibrous dysplasia; an adolescent with segmental pigmentation, pain and MRI-confirmed fibrous dysplasia after negative blood and skin testing; and a girl with very early gonadotropin-independent precocious puberty, transient hepatobiliary abnormalities and positive GNAS testing from a café-au-lait macule but no MRI evidence of fibrous dysplasia.
CONCLUSIONS: MAS is a dynamic multisystem mosaic disorder in which manifestations may emerge at different ages and in no fixed order. Negative blood testing does not exclude the diagnosis. Longitudinal endocrine, skeletal, ophthalmological and multidisciplinary surveillance is essential, and treatment should be directed at both endocrine control and preservation of skeletal function.

title: The beneficial impact of a lifestyle modification program on childhood obesity: a comparative study of demographic, anthropometric, and social factors over a decade.
abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Juvenile obesity is a major risk factor for the development of type 2 diabetes. KiCK is a 1-year outpatient pediatric obesity therapy program at the AUF DER BULT Children's and Youth Hospital. In addition to multiprofessional obesity training, clinical and laboratory data are collected at the beginning and end of the program, and a standardized 6-min walking test (6MWT) is carried out.
METHODS: BMI, laboratory parameters, daily media usage time, and the data of the 6-MWT of the program participants in the years 2009-2012 ("A"), 2012-2015 ("B"), and 2018-2019 ("C") were recorded, and the differences between the three groups were analyzed.
RESULTS: Group A included n=64 children (mean age 12.0; 40.6 % female), group B included n=104 children (mean age 11.7; 55.8 % female), and group C included n=131 children (mean age 11.9; 58 % female). BMI-SDS improved constantly in all three groups (A: 2.4 vs. 2.3 (p=0.009); B: 2.4 vs. 2.2 (p=0.003); C: 2.4 vs. 2.1 (p=0.001)). Obesity therapy significantly improved the walking distance in group B in the 6-MWT (B: 574 m vs. 621 m (p=<0.001)).
CONCLUSIONS: The significant improvement in BMI-SDS over decades shows the constant program's contribution to improved weight outcomes in children and adolescents during the periods studied.

title: Hypothalamic astrocytes fine-tune the signals governing metabolism.
abstract: Astrocytes are known to have key roles in the neuroendocrine control of metabolism. The spectrum of actions of this cell population continues to expand as their heterogeneity is deciphered and new study approaches are employed. Astrocytes were first implicated in metabolic control when they were shown to participate in hypothalamic inflammation induced by high-fat diets, which leads to complications such as continued weight gain and glucose intolerance. In addition to their participation in pathophysiological processes associated with poor nutrition and obesity, these glial cells are now accepted as fundamental players in the physiological control of energy homeostasis. Along with their effect on neurons controlling appetite and energy expenditure, glial cells are implicitly involved in the generation of circadian rhythms, including eating and sleep patterns that affect metabolism and may link metabolism with other neuroendocrine systems such as puberty. The evolving concepts regarding astrocytes in metabolic control, including their participation in responses to currently used obesity drugs, highlight them as potential therapeutic targets. Here, we review advances in our understanding of how astrocytes participate in these processes, describe the mechanisms involved and discuss future directions.

title: Impact of surgical versus spontaneous fetal reduction on maternal and neonatal outcomes after assisted reproductive technology: a single-center cohort study of 1, 451 singleton live births.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare maternal and neonatal outcomes among pregnancies with surgical reduction, spontaneous reduction, and initial singleton pregnancies following assisted reproductive technology (ART), and to identify independent risk factors for adverse obstetric outcomes.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 1,451 singleton live births after ART at a single center from January 2018 to December 2023. Participants were divided into three groups: surgical reduction (n=128), spontaneous reduction (n=156), and initial singleton control group (n=1,167). Baseline characteristics, maternal complications, and neonatal outcomes were compared. Multivariate logistic regression was performed to identify independent risk factors.
RESULTS: Univariate analysis revealed significant intergroup differences in the incidence of gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) and preterm birth. The GDM rate was highest in the spontaneous reduction group (26.92%), followed by the surgical reduction group (19.53%) and singleton controls (15.94%, P = 0.003). Preterm birth also differed significantly across groups (19.23% vs 14.06% vs 11.83%, P = 0.024). No group differences were detected for hypertensive disorders of pregnancy, placental complications, or congenital birth defects. After adjusting for maternal age, pre-pregnancy BMI, embryo type, No. of embryos transferred and embryo stage, multivariate logistic regression showed that surgical reduction (OR = 1.22, 95%CI 0.98-1.52, P = 0.069) and spontaneous reduction (OR = 1.39, 95%CI 0.98-1.98, P = 0.067) were not independent risk factors for GDM. Advanced maternal age (OR = 1.12, 95%CI 1.01-1.23, P = 0.028) and elevated pre-pregnancy BMI (OR = 1.11, 95%CI 1.01-1.21, P = 0.030) were the only independent predictors of GDM. For preterm birth, both surgical reduction (OR = 1.35, 95%CI 1.09-1.68, P = 0.007) and spontaneous reduction (OR = 1.72, 95%CI 1.20-2.45, P = 0.003) were independently associated with higher odds of preterm birth. Although the adjusted OR was numerically higher for spontaneous reduction than for surgical reduction, a direct comparison between the two methods showed no statistically significant difference.
CONCLUSION: In ART singleton live births, a history of fetal reduction (surgical or spontaneous) was not independently associated with GDM, but both reduction modalities were independently associated with higher odds of preterm birth.

title: Altered umbilical cord adipokine profile associated with maternal obesity: an exploratory cohort study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Maternal obesity is associated with adverse pregnancy outcomes and may influence fetal metabolic programming through alterations in the intrauterine environment. While leptin has been extensively investigated in pregnancies complicated by maternal obesity, the contribution of emerging adipokines, including neuregulin-4 (NRG4) and isthmin-1 (ISM1), to the fetal adipokine profile remains incompletely understood. This study aimed to characterize alterations in the umbilical cord blood adipokine profile associated with maternal obesity and to evaluate their relationship with early neonatal outcomes.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This prospective exploratory cohort study was conducted at Balıkesir University Faculty of Medicine Hospital, Balıkesir, Türkiye, and included 82 term singleton pregnancies delivered by cesarean section between March and May 2026. Participants were classified as obese (first-trimester BMI ≥30 kg/m², n=40) or non-obese (BMI <30 kg/m², n=42). Maternal demographic and biochemical characteristics, together with neonatal clinical outcomes, were recorded. Umbilical cord blood leptin, NRG4, and ISM1 concentrations were measured using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA). Between-group comparisons, partial correlation analysis, multivariate analysis of covariance (MANCOVA), and analysis of covariance (ANCOVA) were performed.
RESULTS: Maternal glucose concentrations were significantly higher, whereas neonatal glucose concentrations were significantly lower, in the obese group (p = 0.009 and p < 0.001, respectively). Compared with the non-obese group, cord blood leptin and ISM1 concentrations were significantly increased, while NRG4 concentrations were significantly decreased (all p < 0.05). MANCOVA demonstrated a significant overall effect of maternal obesity on the adipokine profile, with leptin contributing most strongly to this association. Following adjustment, leptin remained independently associated with maternal obesity (ANCOVA: p < 0.001, η² = 0.28), whereas ISM1 and NRG4 were no longer independently significant. Partial correlation analysis demonstrated positive associations among the investigated adipokines, with the strongest correlation observed between ISM1 and NRG4 (r = 0.88, p < 0.001). No significant differences were observed between the groups regarding neonatal complications, Apgar scores, umbilical cord blood pH, lactate, bilirubin concentrations, or neonatal intensive care unit admission.
CONCLUSION: Maternal obesity was associated with an altered umbilical cord adipokine profile characterized by a robust increase in leptin together with coordinated alterations in emerging adipokines. Although these biochemical changes were not accompanied by differences in early neonatal outcomes, they may represent early metabolic adaptations to an obesogenic intrauterine environment. These findings support the potential role of cord blood adipokines as biomarkers of fetal metabolic programming and warrant confirmation in larger prospective longitudinal studies.

title: Growth Hormone Stimulation Testing in Childhood: Diagnostic Pathways and Discordant Results in a Tertiary Centre Cohort.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Growth hormone stimulation tests (GHSTs) are central to the diagnosis of growth hormone deficiency (GHD) despite recognised limitations. Two failed GHSTs are recommended to confirm GHD; however, a single failed test may be considered sufficient in selected cases. This study aimed to describe GHST practice in a tertiary paediatric endocrine centre, to determine how often an initial subthreshold GHST was not followed by a final diagnosis of GHD and to assess the diagnostic performance of IGF-I, IGFBP-3 and the IGF-I/IGFBP-3 molar ratio.
DESIGN: Retrospective observational study.
PATIENTS: Seventy-three children who underwent GHST for suspected GHD at a tertiary Irish paediatric endocrinology centre.
MEASUREMENTS: Clinical, biochemical and radiological data were reviewed, including height, BMI, height velocity, IGF-I, IGFBP-3, bone age and GHST results.
RESULTS: GHD was diagnosed in 34 children (47%) and excluded in 39 (53%). Of 47 children with a first peak GH below 7 µg/L, GHD was subsequently excluded in 13, an apparent false-positive rate of 27.7% (95% CI 16.9-41.8). Six of the 13 had a severely subthreshold initial response (peak GH < 3 µg/L). Discordant results were clustered in peripubertal children. IGF-I had poor sensitivity and specificity (45.5% and 50.0%, respectively); IGFBP-3 had low sensitivity but high specificity (9.1% and 100%, respectively). The IGF-I/IGFBP-3 molar ratio did not differ between diagnostic groups.
CONCLUSIONS: Approximately one in four children with a subthreshold first GHST was not ultimately diagnosed with GHD. These findings support the need for repeat testing before initiating treatment in children without independent evidence of pituitary disease.

Clinical Guidance for Disease-Modifying Immunotherapy in Children and Adolescents With New-Onset (Stage 3) Type 1 Diabetes.
abstract: The 2026 U.S. approval of teplizumab, for children and adolescents aged 8-17 years with recently diagnosed stage 3 type 1 diabetes, changes the first weeks after diagnosis. Clinicians must treat hyperglycemia and teach lifelong care skills while considering whether to preserve residual β-cell function. Teplizumab is the current clinical exemplar, although the implementation challenges extend beyond one agent. This article addresses who should lead care, how to approach eligibility and timing, how to assess β-cell reserve and infection risk, how to sequence treatment with diabetic ketoacidosis recovery and early education, and how to monitor treatment safely. Teplizumab-specific recommendations are identified, with broader principles framed for adaptation across health systems.

title: Nonlinear associations of bone age and basal luteinizing hormone with uterine volume in girls with central precocious puberty: a segmented regression analysis.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: The relationships between basal luteinizing hormone (LH), bone age (BA), and uterine volume in girls with precocious puberty are conventionally treated as linear in clinical practice. Whether these associations exhibit nonlinear, threshold-dependent patterns has not been formally investigated.
METHODS: This retrospective cross-sectional study included 1, 617 girls with breast development before 8 years of age, of whom 1, 008 had central precocious puberty (CPP) and 609 had premature thelarche (PT). Restricted cubic spline regression was used to test for nonlinearity in the associations of BA and ln-transformed basal LH with ln-transformed uterine volume. Where nonlinearity was confirmed, piecewise linear regression identified breakpoints at which uterine growth accelerated. CPP girls were then cross-classified by the identified thresholds to evaluate their complementary value.
RESULTS: CPP girls had significantly greater BA advancement than PT girls (1.87 ± 1.11 vs. 1.58 ± 1.02 years, P < 0.001). In CPP girls, both BA and basal LH exhibited significant nonlinear associations with uterine volume (both P < 0.0001). A BA breakpoint was identified at 10.6 years: below this threshold, each additional year was associated with a 0.067-unit increase in ln(uterine volume); above 10.6 years, the slope increased to 0.550 (8.2-fold acceleration, P < 0.001). A basal LH breakpoint was identified at 0.67 IU/L, below which the slope was 0.107 per ln-unit and above which it rose to 0.421 (3.9-fold acceleration, P < 0.001). In PT girls, no clinically meaningful breakpoints were found. When CPP girls were stratified by both thresholds, the "Both High" subgroup (16.5%) had a median uterine volume of 2.76 mL (47.6% exceeding 3.0 mL), compared with 1.22 mL (1.4%) in the "Both Low" subgroup (58.6%).
CONCLUSIONS: The associations of BA and basal LH with uterine volume in CPP are distinctly nonlinear, with identifiable thresholds beyond which uterine growth accelerates substantially. These breakpoints are proposed as quantitative descriptors of uterine maturation tempo rather than as diagnostic cutoffs; they have high specificity but limited sensitivity, and girls with values below the thresholds require clinical follow-up. These two indicators provide complementary information for characterizing the tempo of uterine maturation.

title: Twelve novel Italian cases of hypophosphatasia: challenging cases with an extremely variable phenotype.
abstract:
CONTEXT: Hypophosphatasia (HPP) is an inborn error of bone metabolism affecting the musculoskeletal and nervous systems. It is caused by monoallelic or biallelic pathogenic variants of the ALPL gene, which encodes the tissue non-specific alkaline phosphatase (TNSAP). Given its marked clinical variability ranging from prenatal presentations to symptoms onset in late adulthood, HPP often runs undetected with potential harms for affected individuals.
METHODS: Clinical, molecular, in silico, in vitro, and, when accessible, family studies were carried out on 12 HPP individuals with variable clinical presentations. Variants were classified according to the American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics recommendations.
RESULTS: Four cases were diagnosed as infantile, one as adult HPP. The other cases were completely asymptomatic (nr 4) or showed symptoms not strictly HPP-related (nr 3) but were all identified incidentally based on the biochemical low ALP value or severe bone fragility phenotype. Twelve "pathogenic o likely pathogenic variants" were identified including 9 missense (1 novel, 8 previously reported), 2 in frame indels and one multiexonic deletion. In vitro characterization of the seven point variants without previously described functional data confirmed a dramatic decreased enzymatic activity of some mutated enzymes.
CONCLUSIONS: Improving the recognition of HPP is essential because its rarity and extreme variable presentation with many asymptomatic cases lead to misdiagnosis or delay. Increased clinical awareness and attention to persistently low ALP levels are crucial to achieve earlier and more accurate diagnosis.

title: The developmental, genetic, and epigenetic basis of polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome.
abstract: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is the most common reproductive and endocrine disorder affecting women in their reproductive age. PCOS is characterized by clustering of reproductive disturbances, including, but not limited to, hypothalamus-pituitary-ovarian axis dysfunction, chronic anovulation, excess androgen, and subfertility. PCOS extends beyond reproductive dysfunction to involve metabolic, endocrine, and cardiometabolic abnormalities. Therefore, it has recently been redefined as polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS). Despite the evolution of diagnostic criteria for PMOS in recent decades, there persists a knowledge gap regarding its origins and pathophysiology. Genetic studies have identified candidate genes associated with PMOS, but genetic factors alone cannot account for its varied phenotypes. The diverse phenotypes observed in PMOS instead point to a complex gene-environment interaction, thereby paving the way for epigenetic mechanisms to explain this heterogeneous trait. Emerging evidence suggests that epigenetic alterations during critical developmental periods, particularly in utero and during puberty, may contribute to the reproductive, metabolic, and endocrine manifestations of PMOS. These observations may re-frame PMOS as a developmental disorder that follows the developmental origin of health and disease (DOHaD) theory. In this review, we propose a comprehensive framework to address the complexity of PMOS pathogenesis and phenotypes. We investigated how environmental exposures during critical windows may shape the epigenome and contribute to PMOS development. The review also examines the biological rationale of the 2023 International Evidence-based Guideline for PCOS, including the use of anti-Müllerian hormone, postponing diagnosis until after puberty, and recommendations for healthy lifestyle behaviors.
keywords: developmental origin of health and disease (DOHaD)

title: Maternal psychological distress and child psychosocial functioning in girls with central precocious puberty: a prospective study before and after GnRH analogue treatment.
abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Central precocious puberty (CPP) may have psychosocial implications for girls and their mothers. We evaluated changes in maternal psychological distress during gonadotropin-releasing hormone analogue (GnRHa) therapy and associations with child emotional, behavioral, and peer-related functioning.
METHODS: This prospective observational study included 40 girls with confirmed CPP and their mothers. Eligibility required documented progressive breast development before age 8, clinical progression, and biochemical central activation; isolated thelarche, isolated pubarche, and lipomastia were excluded. Child psychosocial measures and baseline maternal Depression Anxiety Stress Scale-21 (DASS-21) were completed at the same visit. Maternal DASS-21 was repeated at variable times during ongoing GnRHa therapy.
RESULTS: Mean total maternal DASS-21 score decreased from 13.38 ± 10.58 to 7.13 ± 8.15 (p<0.001). Maternal total DASS-21 showed moderate positive associations with total internalizing symptoms (ρ=0.501, p<0.001) and several RCADS-P domains; the total internalizing association remained after adjustment for BMI SDS (partial ρ=0.510, p<0.001). Among behavioral and social outcomes, maternal total DASS-21 was associated with hyperactivity, while exploratory maternal anxiety analyses showed associations with the ADHD Index and hyperactivity. DASS-21 change was not associated with age at diagnosis or reassessment interval.
CONCLUSIONS: Maternal psychological distress decreased over time during GnRHa therapy and showed moderate associations with mother-reported emotional symptoms in girls with confirmed CPP. These findings support individualized, family-centered psychosocial assessment as part of CPP care.

title: ENPP1 deficiency in siblings with apparently discordant phenotypes: case report and a review of the literature.
abstract:
OBJECTIVES: ENPP1 deficiency encompasses a phenotypic spectrum from generalized arterial calcification of infancy (GACI) to autosomal recessive hypophosphatemic rickets type 2 (ARHR2), and phenotypic variability has been reported even among individuals carrying the same variants; however, the extent of intrafamilial phenotypic concordance remains unclear.
CASE PRESENTATION: Case 1, a 20-month-old boy, presented with genu varum and fibroblast growth factor 23-mediated hypophosphatemic rickets. Genetic testing identified compound heterozygous ENPP1 variants, c.937_938insT (p.Gln313LeufsTer18), and a deletion involving exons 8-13. Ultrasonography revealed valvular calcifications, carotid intimal irregularity, and nephrocalcinosis. Case 2, his younger brother, developed fetal hydrops, diffuse cardiovascular calcification, and severe cardiac dysfunction in late gestation and died shortly after preterm birth. Postmortem examination demonstrated extensive vascular calcification consistent with GACI; genetic testing identified the same variants. A sibling-based literature review of genetically confirmed cases with shared biallelic ENPP1 variants identified 21 publications describing 26 unrelated families. Including the present family, 27 families comprising 61 affected individuals were analyzed; 24 families (88.9 %) had concordant phenotypes, whereas three (11.1 %) had discordant phenotypes. Among 19 individuals who presented with hypophosphatemia or ARHR2 without a documented history of GACI and underwent cardiovascular, calcification, and/or hearing assessment, 14 had abnormal findings.
CONCLUSIONS: Documented GACI status was generally concordant among affected siblings. Frequent cardiovascular, calcification-related, and/or hearing abnormalities in patients presenting with hypophosphatemia or ARHR2 without a documented history of GACI highlight the importance of multisystem assessment and support GACI and ARHR2 as overlapping manifestations within the ENPP1 deficiency spectrum.

title: Current Diabetes Technologies and Everyday School Life of Children and Adolescents with Type 1 Diabetes: Did We Do Our Homework?
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Automated insulin delivery (AID) systems have been rapidly adopted among children and adolescents with type 1 diabetes (T1D) in Germany. This study aimed to evaluate the impact of AID use on glycemic control, school participation, and parental burden.
METHODS: A cross-sectional multicenter survey was conducted among parents of school-aged children (6-16 years). Participants completed questionnaires covering demographic and clinical characteristics, diabetes support during school hours, participation in school activities, and school-related disruptions (calls, pick-ups).
RESULTS: A total of 775 parents participated (77.6% mothers); children attended primary (n = 203), secondary (n = 554) and special needs schools (n = 13). Among primary school children, 76% received external support during school hours. Although secondary school students were more likely to participate in school activities, 10%-28% of them and 24%-61% of primary school students were still unable to participate in certain activities. HbA1c levels were lower among AID users; however, AID use did not improve participation and was associated with more frequent school phone calls (p = .042) and early pick-ups (p < .001). Approximately one-third of parents reduced their working hours immediately following their child's diabetes diagnosis.
CONCLUSIONS: Despite a well-resourced healthcare system, schools lack integrated standardized diabetes support. Although AID use improved glycemic control, this did not translate into better school participation and was associated with increased school-related contacts, suggesting a shift in burden to parents, possibly due to insufficient support for AID use in school. Structured, integrated support adapted to new diabetes technologies is needed.

title: Case Report: KBG syndrome in an adult presenting with diabetes, gout, and hypogonadism.
abstract: KBG syndrome (MIM #148050) is an autosomal dominant disorder caused by pathogenic variants in ANKRD11 or 16q24.3 microdeletions, classically recognized in children through macrodontia, short stature, skeletal anomalies, and neurodevelopmental delay. How the syndrome presents to adult internal medicine remains poorly documented. A 31-year-old man was admitted with new-onset diabetes (blood glucose 20.0 mmol/L) and an acute gout flare, superimposed on congenital sensorineural deafness, repaired cryptorchidism, and 10 years of recurrent gout. Examination revealed macrodontia of the upper central incisors, kyphoscoliosis, brachydactyly with fifth-finger clinodactyly, bilateral gynecomastia, and small soft testes. Investigations showed preserved β-cell reserve with delayed insulin and C-peptide peaks, negative islet autoantibodies, repeatedly borderline-low testosterone with inadequately normal gonadotropins, and 24-h urinary uric acid excretion at the lower end of the reference range. Maternally inherited diabetes and deafness was initially suspected because diabetes coexisted with deafness, but the burden of congenital anomalies prompted trio whole-exome sequencing, which identified a de novo heterozygous ANKRD11 frameshift (NM_013275.6: c.1903_1907del, p.Lys635Glnfs*26). He was treated with liraglutide, febuxostat, colchicine, and atorvastatin. Over 33 months of follow-up, glycated hemoglobin remained between 4.5% and 5.3% and thyroid function normalized, yet serum urate stayed markedly elevated at nearly every routine measurement, and one gout flare required readmission. This case illustrates delayed recognition of KBG syndrome during adulthood: the characteristic dental, skeletal, and developmental signs had been present since early childhood, yet the syndrome was named only when an acquired metabolic cluster-diabetes, gout, and hypogonadism-brought him to adult endocrine care. The decade of gout preceding glucose intolerance is, to our knowledge, the first such report in KBG syndrome and remains a single observation; whether it reflects an intrinsic urate-handling defect is a hypothesis that merits further study rather than an established association. Careful attention to dental, skeletal, and developmental clues in atypical diabetes can end a long diagnostic odyssey.

title: Brain MRI Findings and Factor Associated With Clinical Significant CNS Lesions in Girls Aged 6-8 With Central Precocious Puberty.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is recommended for selected girls with central precocious puberty (CPP). Routine brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) in girls aged 6-8 years with central precocious puberty (CPP) remains clinically controversial. Neurological features may help identify girls at higher risk, but whether basal luteinizing hormone (LH), a routinely measured marker of hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis activation, provides additional information beyond age at diagnosis remains uncertain.
METHODS: In this retrospective cross-sectional study, 848 girls aged 6-8 years diagnosed with CPP underwent brain MRI at Vietnam National Children's Hospital between April 2021 and June 2026. Brain MRI findings were classified as clinically significant/pathological, uncertain/questionable significance, or incidental. Neurological characteristics were compared across the MRI categories. Logistic regression was used to identify factors associated with clinically significant MRI abnormalities. Sequential models evaluated whether basal LH provided additional information beyond age at diagnosis, with model fit and discrimination assessed using likelihood-ratio tests, Akaike information criterion (AIC) and area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC).
RESULTS: Any brain MRI abnormalities were identified in 86 girls (10.1%), including 30 (3.5%) with clinically significant central nervous system (CNS) lesions, 14 (1.7%) with questionable findings and 42 (5.0%) with incidental findings. Neurological symptoms, signs or previous CNS history were more frequent among girls with clinically significant abnormalities than among those with uncertain or incidental findings (30.0%, 7.1% and 4.8%, respectively; p = 0.012). Basal LH was independently associated with clinically significant MRI abnormalities (adjusted OR 1.30 per IU/L, 95% CI 1.14-1.47; p < 0.001. Adding basal LH to age at diagnosis significantly improved model fit (AIC 247.79 vs. 259.78; likelihood-ratio p = 0.0002), although discrimination remained modest (AUC 0.654 vs. 0.550 for age alone, p = 0.055). Bone-age advancement did not provide significant additional information.
CONCLUSIONS: In girls aged 6-8 years with CPP, brain MRI abnormalities were identified in approximately 1 in 10 girls, but most were incidental or of uncertain clinical significance. Clinically significant abnormalities were enriched among girls with neurological features. Basal LH provided incremental information beyond age at diagnosis but had limited discriminatory performance. These findings support a risk-stratified approach to brain MRI in girls aged 6-8 years with CPP, with careful neurological assessment remaining central to imaging decisions.
keywords: clinically significant central nervous system lesions

title: Assessing the Utility of a Capillary-Adjusted Oral Glucose Tolerance Test for the Early Detection of Type 1 Diabetes in Childhood.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The oral glucose tolerance test (OGTT) is the gold standard for staging and monitoring type 1 diabetes (T1D), but it requires venous sampling in a health care setting, limiting its accessibility. We assessed the utility of a capillary-adjusted OGTT (cOGTT) method in children and young people (CYP).
METHODS: Study 1-OGTT method comparison: CYP across the glycemic range underwent contemporaneous venous (vGluc) and capillary (cGluc) glucose sampling at 0-min, 60-min (subgroup), and 120-min after a standard oral glucose load. Agreement between vGluc and cGluc was assessed using Bland-Altman between 3.5 and 15 mmol/L. Glycemic status was assessed using established thresholds and acceptability by questionnaire. Study 2-At-home OGTT feasibility: CYP with early-stage T1D undertook home cOGTT testing (0, 120 min) and completed acceptability questionnaires.
RESULTS: Study 1: Forty-five CYP participated (mean [SD] age 12.2 [3.2] years; range 5-17), with 20 undergoing additional 60-min sampling. cGluc and vGluc showed reasonable agreement across the glycemic range of 3.5-15 mmol/L, (bias, -0.22 mmol/L; 95% confidence interval [CI]: -0.51 to 0.07; 95% limits of agreement, -2.91 to 2.47 mmol/L). cGluc performed well at normoglycemia: 21/22 (95% sensitivity; 95% CI: 77%-100%), 14/17 (82% specificity; 57%-96%); and hyperglycemia: 9/10 (90% sensitivity; 55%-100%), 29/29 (100% specificity; 88%-100%); but less well for dysglycemia: 4/7 (57% sensitivity; 18%-90%), 30/32 (94% specificity; 79%-99%). In 76% (32/42), cOGTT was preferred for future testing. Study 2: 45 CYP participated (10.4 [3.1] years; range 4-17). In 91% (41/45), home cOGTT tests were completed successfully (3 device failures, 1 incomplete test). Home testing was acceptable in 98% (44 of 45). Two CYP were identified with stage 3 T1D with no evidence of DKA.
CONCLUSIONS: The cOGTT method is feasible and acceptable compared with venous OGTT in CYP, with promising performance for detecting hyperglycemia, but further assessment is needed before it can be used for glycemic staging.

title: Gut microbiota dysbiosis and altered short-chain fatty acid biosynthetic pathways in Chinese children with obesity and nonalcoholic fatty liver disease.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Nonalcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD), recently reclassified as metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), is the most prevalent chronic liver disease in children, affecting 13% of the general pediatric population and up to 47% of children with obesity worldwide. Gut microbiota dysbiosis contributes to NAFLD pathogenesis through the gut-liver axis, yet the interplay between microbial communities and host metabolic regulators, particularly angiopoietin-like protein 4 (ANGPTL4), remains incompletely characterized.
METHODS: Eighty-nine Chinese children aged 5-15 years were enrolled, including 29 healthy controls (Con), 39 with simple obesity (OB), and 21 with obesity and NAFLD. Gut microbiota was profiled by 16S rRNA gene sequencing (V3-V4 region) and analyzed using QIIME2 and MicrobiomeAnalyst. Functional prediction employed PICRUSt2 referencing MetaCyc pathways. Serum ANGPTL4, leptin, adiponectin, and interleukin-6 were measured.
RESULTS: Chao1 species richness differed significantly among groups (F = 4.98, p = 0.009), while Shannon diversity did not (F = 2.22, p = 0.115). Beta diversity (PERMANOVA, F = 2.87, R2 = 0.063, p = 0.002) differed significantly among groups, although PERMDISP indicated heterogeneous dispersion (F = 6.62, p = 0.002). LEfSe analysis identified enrichment of short-chain fatty acid (SCFA)-producing genera (Bacteroides, Alistipes, Oscillospira, Parabacteroides) in healthy controls, while Megamonas, Blautia, Coprococcus, and Dorea characterized the NAFLD group. ANCOM-BC2 identified significant enrichment of Megamonas in the NAFLD group (q = 0.005 vs Con). PICRUSt2 predicted lower abundance of nine SCFA-related pathways in the obesity groups compared with controls. After FDR correction, Bacteroides-ANGPTL4 was the most significant correlation (r = 0.460, q < 0.001), and four additional associations survived correction. In hierarchical regression, Bacteroides remained independently associated with ANGPTL4 after adjustment for age, BMI, sex, and Tanner stage (β = 0.254, p = 0.016, ΔR2 = 0.057), although this association was attenuated after additional adjustment for group status (β = 0.204, p = 0.058).
CONCLUSION: Chinese children with obesity and NAFLD exhibit gut microbial dysbiosis characterized by reduced species richness, depletion of SCFA-producing genera, and lower predicted abundance of SCFA-related pathways. The independent association between Bacteroides and ANGPTL4 suggests a potential microbiota-host metabolic link that may be associated with hepatic lipid metabolism.

title: Is polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome a legacy of excessive gestational weight gain? A review of developmental and transgenerational programming.
abstract: Polyendocrine Metabolic Ovarian Syndrome (PMOS), formerly known as Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (PCOS), is increasingly recognized as a systemic endocrine-metabolic disorder characterized by hyperandrogenism, ovulatory dysfunction, insulin resistance, adipose tissue dysfunction, and hypothalamic-pituitary-ovarian (HPO) axis alterations. Evidence suggests susceptibility may originate before reproductive maturity, potentially during fetal development. This review examines whether excessive gestational weight gain (EGWG) elevates offspring PMOS risk through developmental (intergenerational and, potentially, transgenerational) endocrine programming. EGWG, defined as weight gain above the recommended range for prepregnancy body mass index, may reflect heterogeneous changes in maternal and fetal tissues rather than excess maternal fat accumulation alone. In some pregnancies, EGWG co-occurs with insulin resistance, altered lipid metabolism, inflammation, or adipokine dysregulation. These changes could modify placental nutrient transfer and endocrine signaling, thereby influencing offspring metabolic and reproductive development. However, the pathways linking EGWG specifically to PMOS remain uncertain. Human studies associate maternal metabolic conditions and PMOS with selected offspring outcomes, but provide limited evidence that EGWG independently predicts PMOS in daughters. Experimental models show that prenatal androgen exposure and maternal dietary perturbations can produce PCOS-like reproductive and metabolic traits, supporting the biological plausibility of developmental programming. This review evaluates whether EGWG may act as a marker or modifier of intrauterine conditions relevant to later PMOS susceptibility, while considering prepregnancy adiposity, maternal PMOS, genetic predisposition, and postnatal exposures as alternative or interacting explanations. Prospective mother-daughter cohorts with repeated pregnancy measures, placental profiling, and follow-up through puberty and adulthood are needed to test this hypothesis.

title: Case Report: Acute liver injury with Epstein-Barr virus DNAemia following teplizumab: drug-induced liver injury, viral reactivation, or both?
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Teplizumab (anti-CD3) delays progression from stage 2 to stage 3 type 1 diabetes (T1D) but can be associated with laboratory abnormalities and virologic findings, including Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) DNAemia.
METHODS: We report a 15-year-old boy with stage 2 T1D who received a standard course of teplizumab and developed a biphasic rise in aminotransferases occurring mainly after the end of infusions, with preserved bilirubin and coagulation parameters.
RESULTS: During treatment, ALT/AST rose to 78/44 U/L (1.90/1.10×ULN). After completion, ALT/AST increased to 292/172 U/L (7.12/4.30×ULN) on post-treatment day +5 and peaked at 428/220 U/L (10.44/5.50×ULN) on day +6, followed by partial improvement and a second flare beginning on day +20 and peaking on day +24 (ALT 293 U/L, 7.15×ULN; AST 118 U/L, 2.95×ULN; GGT 142 U/L), with normal bilirubin. Coagulation parameters remained within the normal range. Work-up for autoimmune hepatitis, hepatitis B/C, CMV, adenovirus, parvovirus B19, and toxoplasmosis was negative. Abdominal ultrasound/Doppler was unremarkable. MRI reported liver size mildly increased/at the upper limit of normal, nonspecific segment IV abnormalities, and reactive abdominal lymph nodes, with interval improvement at follow-up. Pre-treatment VCA IgG was positive and VCA IgM negative. At post-treatment day +10, whole-blood EBV DNA was 538,623 copies/mL, with negative VCA IgM, EA IgG and EBNA IgG, decreasing to <200 copies/mL at 6 months. Liver enzymes normalized spontaneously over follow-up.
CONCLUSION: This case highlights marked, biphasic liver injury occurring after teplizumab in association with marked EBV DNAemia. The available clinical, serological, virological, and medication-timing data do not permit definitive attribution to teplizumab, EBV-related hepatic involvement, or concomitant medications. Post-treatment monitoring of both liver enzymes and EBV DNA may be helpful.

title: Psychological care of children, adolescents and young adults with diabetes.
abstract: The 2026 International Society for Pediatric and Adolescent Diabetes (ISPAD) Clinical Practice Consensus Guidelines on psychological care provide updated, evidence-informed recommendations to support the psychological well-being and quality of life of children, adolescents, and young adults living with diabetes. This update adopts a broader biopsychosocial-spiritual and social ecological framework, recognizing the influence of individual, family, cultural, socioeconomic, and environmental factors on psychological health and diabetes outcomes. A major addition is the consideration of psychological aspects of type 1 diabetes screening, early detection, and staging, including parental anxiety, decision-making, and psychological support during ongoing monitoring. The guidelines also expand their coverage of psychological comorbidities, disordered eating behaviors and eating disorders, neurodevelopmental conditions, parental mental health, transition to adult care, and the broader social impact of diabetes, with particular attention to stigma and health equity. Updated recommendations emphasize the integration of routine psychosocial monitoring and screening into diabetes care, including the use of person-reported outcome measures, caregiver assessment, and stepped-care pathways for identifying and addressing psychological difficulties. The guidelines further highlight the importance of developmentally appropriate, person-centered, culturally sensitive, and multidisciplinary approaches to psychological care. By integrating psychological assessment and support into routine diabetes management, these recommendations aim to promote psychological well-being, strengthen family support, and improve the quality of care for young people living with diabetes across diverse healthcare settings.
